dedupe_keys.name: census planning database pdb tract and block group

description: The Planning Database (PDB) of the U.S. Census Bureau is a ready-made table of selected operational, housing, demographic and socio-economic statistics from the decennial census and the American Community Survey 5-year files, for every census tract and block group in the country. It includes the Low Response Score, a predicted rate of not self-responding to a census, plus variables such as housing units, vacancy, renter occupancy, crowding, language, age, income and internet access. The 2026 PDB, published on 4 August 2026 and reissued on 17 September 2026 after an error in the Low Response Score was fixed, uses 2020-2024 ACS 5-year estimates, 2020 Census operational variables and 2020 tract and block group geographies; the tract file has 85,396 rows and 531 columns and the block group file 242,336 rows and 385 columns. Vintages exist for 2015, 2016 and 2018 to 2026. Access: CSV downloads and the Census Data API (pdb group); free and public domain. The Response Outreach Area Mapper shows key PDB statistics on a map. Caveats: designed for survey planning, it repeats ACS estimates without their full margins of error; Excel may truncate the wide files. Simulation uses: a convenient single table of small-area housing and population characteristics for exposure and vulnerability layers, hard-to-reach population mapping for emergency communication, and quick demand baselines. Related records: ACS tables, the 2020 Census DHC and the Community Resilience Estimates.
